_doc: OPS-SHARED-WORKTREE-STATE-REGISTRY-W1 — the SoT for every resource shared ACROSS worktrees on a developer machine. Worktrees isolate the git INDEX and nothing else: $GIT_COMMON_DIR/hooks/*, ~/.crypto-quant-signal/performance.db, the $GIT_COMMON_DIR ledgers and shared deploy checkouts are all common to every checkout. CLAUDE.md's own law — 'a shared primitive gets a CONSUMER REGISTRY, not just drift detection; detection is strictly weaker than enumeration' — was applied to host monitoring artefacts and never to developer-machine state, which is why the 4th writer to pre-push broke every session on 2026-08-01. Read by scripts/check-shared-state.mjs. Missing or unparseable ⇒ SHARED_STATE_VERDICT=INDETERMINATE, exit 3 — never a pass.
_serialization_policy: OPS-SERIALIZE-LANDING-AND-DEPLOY-W1 CH2. Every resource here carries `serialization`: {mechanism, key, scope, _scope_reason}. This registry already enumerated what shared files CONTAIN (sha256) and who WRITES them (writers[]); it had no concept of who may write them AT ONCE — which is the property the observed push livelock and the six unserialized CI workflows both violate. `scope` is MANDATORY and load-bearing: it names the exact boundary within which the mechanism serializes, so the guarantee cannot silently rot when a writer appears outside it. The landing lock serializes ONLY sessions on the one operator Mac sharing $GIT_COMMON_DIR — a second machine, a cloud session, or a GitHub Actions job is outside it, and one of those is not hypothetical (see ref-main). MECHANISMS (five; a sixth needs a wave, not a shrug): `landing-lock` = scripts/lib/with-lock.sh mutual exclusion; `gha-concurrency` = a GitHub Actions top-level concurrency group; `none-single-writer` = exactly one writer, so there is nothing to serialize; `idempotent-composable-write` = N writers, no mutual exclusion, but each write is a whole read-modify-rewrite whose result is a function of OUR ordering rule rather than of writer sequence; `append-atomic` = N writers appending through O_APPEND. The last two were added because two PRE-EXISTING rows already had 3 writers each and their writers are frozen by this wave's firewall. They are DECLARATIONS, not exemptions: an exemption channel is a control later waves widen until the rule is vacuous, whereas a declaration has to state a mechanism and a residual that a reader can check.
_consumers_policy: consumers[] is ENUMERATED, never a count. Where the consumer set is genuinely dynamic (every live worktree governed by a shared hook), the row carries `consumers_derived_from` — the exact command that enumerates it — and check-shared-state.mjs PRINTS the enumeration at runtime. Freezing 75 worktree paths into a committed file would be stale within the hour; a hand-maintained COUNT is forbidden outright (this repo has already had '3 send paths'→8 and '6th consumer'→12 drift unnoticed).
_sha256_policy: ONE canonical sha256 per fact, and for most rows here that hash lives somewhere else already. Repo-tracked scripts are integrity-checked by git itself. The two ops/ artefacts below carry `inventory_ref` because ops/monitoring/monitoring-inventory.json already records their canonical sha256 and reconciles it daily — recording it a second time would be a second thing that can drift, which is the exact failure mode the monitoring-inventory arc codified. The generated hooks are machine-local and rewritten by every install, so a hash of them is meaningless by construction. A null sha256 here always carries its reason.
_skip_ledger_stale_threshold_reason: The skip ledger records a guard that ran nowhere. With 69 of 75 checkouts missing at least one gate script on 2026-08-02, a normal week legitimately produces dozens of rows, so a low threshold would fire constantly and teach the operator to ignore it. 200 flags a genuinely persistent unguarded population without crying wolf during the reclamation backlog. Re-tune when OPS-WORKTREE-RECLAIM-W{NEXT} lands and the population drops.

serialization.scope: the single $GIT_COMMON_DIR/hooks/pre-push file on this machine, across all installers
serialization._scope_reason: No mutual exclusion, and none is needed for the ordinary case: every installer goes through hook_block_install, which splits the file into (foreign remainder + one file per block), replaces its own block keyed on NAME alone, and re-emits in canonical LC_ALL=C order. The result is a function of OUR ordering rule, not of installer sequence, so two installs in either order converge on the same bytes. RESIDUAL, stated rather than hoped away: two installers running SIMULTANEOUSLY are a genuine last-writer-wins race on the read-modify-rewrite, in which the loser's block is dropped. That is detected by this reconciler's MISSING_BLOCK check and recovered from the timestamped .bak the installer takes before its first mutation. Installs are hand-run and rare; the residual is not worth a mutex that every installer would have to be edited to take.

resources.invariant: Refuses HISTORY DESTRUCTION — a non-fast-forward or a deletion — on a ref declared in ops/push-safety-config.json, and, since OPS-PUSH-SAFETY-WIP-NAMESPACE-W1 (2026-08-20), REFUSES any push carrying a ref in a namespace declared local-only in `never_push_refs` — today `refs/algovault/*`, the auto-preserved snapshots of uncommitted work — regardless of whether that push is a clean fast-forward, because there the objection is to the CONTENT leaving a public repo rather than to history being destroyed. Nothing else. Ordinary fast-forward pushes, brand-new branches and every non-protected ref are explicitly allowed: this repo's LAW is auto-commit + auto-push and merges land as fast-forwards, so a conventional main-protection hook would halt every wave. Converts two CLAUDE.md laws ('Never force push to main/master', 'Never reset --hard / push --force / branch -D without auth') from prose into mechanical enforcement — measured 2026-08-02, ZERO of the four then-live blocks read the hook's stdin, so neither law was enforced by anything. _(Scope widened 2026-08-20. The prior text ended 'and NOTHING else', which was true when written; it is corrected rather than left to drift, because a registry invariant that no longer matches the script is how a future wave deletes a load-bearing check believing it was never in scope.)_

serialization.scope: each appender writing one whole record per write() to $GIT_COMMON_DIR/algovault-hook-skip.log
serialization._scope_reason: Every writer opens the ledger in append mode, and POSIX requires that the file offset be set to the end of file ATOMICALLY before each write on an O_APPEND descriptor — so concurrent appenders cannot overwrite one another, and no lock is required. (This is O_APPEND's own guarantee. It is NOT a PIPE_BUF argument: PIPE_BUF bounds atomic writes to pipes and FIFOs and says nothing about a regular file.) RESIDUAL: the guarantee is per write() call, so a writer that emits a record in more than one write() can still interleave with another writer's record. Every appender here emits its row with a single printf, which is one write.

resources.invariant: Reports whether a push is running inside scripts/land.sh's landing lock (LANDING_LOCK_VERDICT=ACQUIRED|BYPASSED). REPORT-ONLY: the emitted invocation ends in `|| true`, so it cannot fail a push by construction. TWO properties are load-bearing and neither is a preference. (1) It sorts FIRST in canonical LC_ALL=C order — before dark-exports — so it reports in milliseconds rather than after the full vitest block. (2) It reads NO stdin, and the invocation redirects </dev/null so draining it is structurally impossible: check-push-safety.sh consumes the hook's stdin to learn which refs are being pushed and PASSes on zero lines, so a block ahead of it that drained stdin would make force-push and deletion protection silently pass. Asserted two ways after install: a fixture force-push still returns PUSH_SAFETY_VERDICT=FAIL, an ordinary fast-forward still returns PASS with '1 ref update(s) checked'. If this detector ever needs ref data, tee in check-push-safety.sh — NEVER reorder.
resources._severity_reason: Report-only is a STAGED control, not a permanent preference. FLIP CRITERION, carrying both a numeric AND a time condition so it cannot become a guard parked in REPORT forever: promote to blocking in OPS-LANDING-LOCK-ENFORCE-W{NEXT} when the BYPASSED count in $GIT_COMMON_DIR/algovault-locks/bypass-ledger.log is ZERO across a continuous 14-day window AND that window has elapsed since install (2026-08-20). Every run appends to the ledger, so the rate is measured rather than guessed at the decision.
resources._report_only_reason: Absence of this block from a worktree costs MEASUREMENT, not protection — it blocks nothing. Declared so UNGUARDED_WORKTREE does not print 'those checkouts have NO protection from this gate at all', which would be a false statement about a detector.

resources.invariant: Every landing runs the ~2-minute pre-push gate EXACTLY ONCE. Before this wave a session that lost the race burned a full gate and re-ran it, so the cost per landing grew with the number of parallel sessions. Measured with a synthetic gate over throwaway repos: at N=4 concurrent sessions the unlocked control took 10 gate executions and 6 non-fast-forward refusals to land 4 changes (2.50 per landing); through scripts/land.sh it took exactly 4, with 0 refusals and every LAND_ATTEMPTS=1.
resources._sha256_reason: A git ref is a moving pointer; a recorded hash of it would be stale on the next push.
resources.notes: The lock lives in scripts/land.sh, NOT in the pre-push hook. git has already computed the refs being pushed by the time a hook runs and a pre-push hook cannot rebase, so a hook-held lock makes the second session wait, run its gate, and still be refused non-fast-forward because it never rebased onto the winner's tip. The critical section must contain the fetch and the rebase.

serialization.scope: sessions on the ONE operator Mac that go through scripts/land.sh, sharing this $GIT_COMMON_DIR
serialization._scope_reason: Within that scope the non-fast-forward race is ELIMINATED, not reduced: land.sh releases only after `git push` returns, and both the gate and the ref transfer run inside that call, so the second session cannot begin its fetch until the first has fully landed and therefore always rebases onto a tip that cannot move under it. There is no residual timing window for participants. THE RESIDUAL IS SCOPE, and all three cases are declared rather than hoped away. (1) A raw `git push` that bypasses land.sh — measured by the bypass-detect block, report-only until its flip criterion is met. (2) A writer OUTSIDE this Mac. This is NOT hypothetical and is the wave's most valuable measurement: .github/workflows/regenerate-landing.yml checks out with a PAT, commits regenerated landing surfaces and `git push`es to main — a local mutex cannot see it, and no concurrency group can make a CI job wait on a laptop's lock. Hardening that writer is OPS-CI-MAIN-WRITER-HARDEN-W{NEXT}, which OWNS this residual; it is recorded on this row rather than in prose so it cannot be forgotten. A second operator machine or a cloud session would land in the same class. (3) A lock TIMEOUT, which fails open by design and says so with a token. land.sh's bounded, jittered rebase-retry is the fail-safe for those three cases ONLY — it is not what makes landing safe, and inside the lock it must never fire.

serialization.scope: all runs of this workflow for ONE tag ref
serialization._scope_reason: PER-REF, and this is the clause that prevents a silent release loss. GitHub cancels a PENDING run when a new run joins the same group; under a global group, tagging v1.2.4 while v1.2.3 was still pending would CANCEL the v1.2.3 publish — a version that never publishes, with no failure anywhere to alarm on. Keying on github.ref makes two versions structurally unable to share a group. Group names are case-insensitive per the GitHub docs, so case must never be the only thing distinguishing two groups.

The >=2-writers rule therefore does not decide these rows — the CI_SERIALIZATION checks do, and they require a non-empty serialization.key on EVERY ci-workflow row regardless of writer count.
resources.invariant: Carries a TOP-LEVEL concurrency block whose group equals serialization.key, with queue: max and NO cancel-in-progress. queue: max (never the `single` default) because waves cite deploy and publish run IDs as acceptance evidence, and a run cancelled while PENDING is not a failure anywhere — it is simply missing. cancel-in-progress is not set on any workflow in this repo: it is the wrong knob for pending-run cancellation (the documented knob is queue), its `false` value appears nowhere in GitHub's documentation, and queue: max combined with cancel-in-progress: true is an explicit workflow validation error.
resources._sha256_reason: Repo-tracked; git is the integrity mechanism.

serialization._scope_reason: contended_target is NONE, stated rather than invented. This workflow's own header says it plainly: 'no build, no image, no SSH, no deploy — a static lint over committed JSON'. It mutates nothing, so it has no shared resource to serialize and the group buys only run-lane dedup. It is registered and grouped ANYWAY because the enumeration clause is what makes a 7th workflow structurally unable to land unserialized — an exempt workflow is a hole in exactly the rule this wave exists to install. An earlier draft of the spec assigned it 'monitoring host'; that was fabricated and is corrected here.

worktree_roots._doc: OPS-WORKTREE-ROOT-CONFINEMENT-W2 CH2. Worktree placement was the last emergent shared resource on this machine: it is CWD-derived and tool-version-dependent (three placements measured inside one 24h window), so it cannot be documented, only DECLARED. Paths are ABSOLUTE — a tilde row matches nothing resolved from `git worktree list --porcelain`, i.e. an exemption that silently does not exist.

repo_root.reason: the ONE repo root; a second root is the duplicate-clone generator (2 live duplicates prove it)

worktree_roots.destination_reason: dot-prefixed so ~/code reads as a plain list of repos; outside every repo tree so the vitest-discovery pathology (1779 discovered test files vs 298 real) is structurally impossible rather than merely detected; promotes the convention 4 worktrees already follow
worktree_roots.payload_floor_reason: 1 MB — 256x above observed noise (a 4 KB .env.local, copied into every worktree by cc-session.sh by design; resolve with `grep -n '.env.local' scripts/cc-session.sh`); 15x below the smallest real payload (15.5 MB). The margin above noise is comfortable; 15x below the smallest payload is tighter than it looks, so anything landing in the band floor -> 15.5 MB REPORTS for human classification rather than passing silently.

payload_report_band_kb.reason: floor -> smallest known real payload (15.5 MB). A worktree in this gap is neither noise nor a known dataset: report it, never auto-classify.

R1_confinement.baseline_note: 35 as check-worktree-root.mjs measures it, 2026-08-09: NON-EXEMPT worktrees outside worktree_root. This is the guard's OWN metric — CH1's raw 40 counted exempt paths too, and a baseline that is not the number the promotion criterion reads is a baseline nobody can compare against. A PREFIX predicate, not a shape predicate: the 4 compliant worktrees are direct children of worktree_root, and an exact <repo>/<task> rule would score them violations too. The population moves (43->48 worktrees during CH2 alone), so this is history, not an expectation — promotion reads max_violations, never this figure.

promotion.decide_by_reason: A TIME BOUND IS A DEADLINE, NOT A DELAY. This was 'not_before: 2026-08-23', which is a WAITING PERIOD — the inverse of what CLAUDE.md's promotion rule asks for. That rule exists because a count-only criterion can never fire if the population never heals, so it wants a date by which somebody DECIDES, not a date before which nobody may act. Corrected by OPS-WORKTREE-ROOT-R2-PROMOTE-W1; the same error is retired from R2_nesting in the same commit.
promotion.reason: count AND deadline. R1 stays report because worktrees outside the root are DIRTY and `git worktree move` refuses a dirty worktree — forcing R1 would mean moving another session's uncommitted work. It heals as sessions land, and the observed count is appended below so the RATE is measured rather than guessed at the decision.

observed.note: baseline as recorded by W2 CH2
OPS-WORKTREE-ROOT-R2-PROMOTE-W1: -30 in one day, so the population IS healing; the waiting-period date was never the constraint

instrument.population: R1_confinement violations — sibling worktrees placed outside the declared worktree_root, counted live per run and appended to observed[] at each decision point.
instrument.written_by: scripts/check-worktree-root.mjs — the subject of this criterion.
instrument.reobserve: Re-take the measurement now with `node scripts/check-worktree-root.mjs` and read the R1 count, or enumerate `git worktree list` and compare each path against worktree_roots.worktree_root. observed[] is a hand-recorded series of past samples, not the population: a past count cannot be recomputed once the worktrees have moved.
instrument.reason: D, not B: the count is external world-state — where the checkouts physically sit — and it is not in git, so no commit re-derives a past value. D, not C: the gate READS placement, so a deliberate run cannot report a worktree outside the root without someone first creating one there; an extra sample is always TRUE and can only make the criterion harder to satisfy, never easier. Added by OPS-PROMOTION-INSTRUMENT-INDEPENDENCE-W1 CH1. This block is NESTED three levels deep, and it is the case that settled R1.4's discovery rule: excluding it for being nested would have been an accident of file layout rather than a principle, and would have handed every future criterion an escape hatch one indent deep.

R2_nesting.predicate: no worktree path inside any primary's or any other worktree's tree
R2_nesting.mode_note: PROMOTED report -> block by OPS-WORKTREE-ROOT-R2-PROMOTE-W1 on 2026-08-10, on BOTH legs re-derived live: violations == 0, AND the blast-radius set (worktrees that would be refused under BLOCK) computed empty from `git worktree list --porcelain` per structurally-discovered primary, independently of this guard. The 2026-08-16 'not_before' was retired as an author error, not satisfied as a criterion — see R1_confinement.promotion.decide_by_reason. PRECONDITION, and it is why R1-of-that-wave shipped first: the WorktreeCreate hook's fail-open used to place at <repo>/.claude/worktrees/<name>, which is itself an R2 violation, so promoting alone would have wired a benign fail-open to a fleet-wide push refusal. That fallback now lands inside worktree_root as _failopen-<task>.
R2_nesting.baseline_note: 10 as the guard measures it, 2026-08-09: non-exempt worktrees inside a primary's or another worktree's tree. All 10 sit in crypto-quant-signal-mcp/.claude/worktrees/. Two of them were generated by the tool WHILE this fix was being planned. R2 is NOT a subset of R1: those paths are under ~/code yet nested.

promoted.rollback: set mode back to "report" and `git revert` the commit — the flip is versioned and fully reversible; a wedged fleet is not, which is why the blast-radius leg gated it

R3_shape.baseline_note: 38 non-exempt worktrees do not match <worktree_root>/<repo>/<task>. Reported, never gated; CH6 drives it to zero.

exempt_paths.reason: OPS-WORKTREE-WORK-PENDING-W1 CH2 R2.3 — de-rents a protection that was a state accident. Dated deliberately: an exemption with no expiry over an artefact that should simply be committed becomes permanent by neglect.
